\chapter{Learning Theory --- Johnson--Lindenstrauss Main}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.LearningTheory.JohnsonLindenstrauss.Main
\section{Overview}

This module assembles the complete Johnson--Lindenstrauss flattening lemma.
Starting from the distortion predicate and the bad-event definitions, it
applies a Gaussian (or sub-Gaussian Rademacher) concentration bound and a
union bound to show, via the probabilistic method, that for any finite set
$V \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ of at most $n$ points and any $0 < \varepsilon < 1$,
a random $k \times d$ matrix with $k \ge 32 \log n / \varepsilon^2$ rows is,
with positive probability, an $\varepsilon$-JL embedding of $V$; it then
extracts the deterministic witness and provides both squared-distance and
distance-form corollaries together with explicit logarithmic dimension bounds.

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Single-pair distortion bound]
\lean{JLDistortion}
\label{JLDistortion}
\leanok
For $\varepsilon \in \mathbb{R}$, vectors $u, v \in \mathbb{R}^d$, and their
images $u', v' \in \mathbb{R}^k$, \texttt{JLDistortion} asserts the two-sided
squared-distance inequality
\[
  (1 - \varepsilon)\,\|u - v\|^2 \;\le\; \|u' - v'\|^2 \;\le\;
  (1 + \varepsilon)\,\|u - v\|^2.
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[$\varepsilon$-JL embedding]
\lean{IsJLEmbedding}
\label{IsJLEmbedding}
\leanok
\uses{JLDistortion}
A linear map $f : \mathbb{R}^d \to_L[\mathbb{R}] \mathbb{R}^k$ is an
\emph{$\varepsilon$-JL embedding} of a finite set $V$ if, for every ordered
pair $(u, v) \in V \times V$, the pair $(f(u), f(v))$ satisfies
\texttt{JLDistortion} $\varepsilon\; u\; v$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Bad-pair event]
\lean{BadPair}
\label{BadPair}
\leanok
\uses{JLDistortion}
Given a $k \times d$ matrix $A$ and a finite set
$V \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$, \texttt{BadPair} $\varepsilon\; V\; A$ holds when
there exists some ordered pair $(u, v) \in V \times V$ whose images under $A$
fail the distortion predicate, i.e.\ the projection distorts that pair by
more than a factor of $\varepsilon$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Johnson–Lindenstrauss concentration for a single vector]
\lean{jl_concentration_single}
\label{jl_concentration_single}
\leanok
\uses{BadSingle, jl_concentration_single_via_chi_squared}
\difficulty{1}
Let $k \ge 1$ and let $A$ be a random $k \times d$ matrix whose entries $A_{ij}$ are
independent Gaussian random variables, each distributed as $\mathcal{N}(0, 1/k)$. Then
for every fixed vector $x \in \bbr^d$ and every $\varepsilon$ with $0 < \varepsilon <
1$, the probability that $A$ distorts the squared norm of $x$ by more than a factor
$\varepsilon$ satisfies
\[
  \bbP\!\left[\, \bigl|\,\|Ax\|^2 - \|x\|^2\,\bigr| > \varepsilon\,\|x\|^2 \,\right]
  \;\le\; 2\,\exp\!\left(-\frac{k\,\varepsilon^2}{8}\right).
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Distortion bound from a controlled single-vector event]
\lean{JLDistortion.of_not_bad}
\label{JLDistortion.of_not_bad}
\leanok
\uses{BadSingle, JLDistortion}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\varepsilon \in \bbr$, let $u, v \in \bbr^d$, and let $A$ be a real $k \times d$
matrix, acting as a linear map $\bbr^d \to \bbr^k$. Suppose the difference $u - v$ does
not trigger the bad distortion event for $A$; that is, the squared-norm distortion of
$u-v$ stays within the allowed band,
\[
  \bigl|\,\norm{A(u-v)}^2 - \norm{u-v}^2\,\bigr| \;\le\; \varepsilon\,\norm{u-v}^2 .
\]
Then the images $Au$ and $Av$ satisfy the two-sided single-pair distortion bound
\[
(1 - \varepsilon)\,\norm{u - v}^2 \;\le\; \norm{Au - Av}^2 \;\le\; (1 +
\varepsilon)\,\norm{u - v}^2 .
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Union bound for Johnson–Lindenstrauss distortion]
\lean{jl_union_bound}
\label{jl_union_bound}
\leanok
\uses{BadPair, BadSingle, JLDistortion.of_not_bad}
\difficulty{5}
Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, and let $A\colon\Omega\to\bbr^{k\times d}$ be
a measurable random $k\times d$ matrix. Fix a finite set $V\subseteq\bbr^d$ and a
parameter $\varepsilon\in\bbr$, and suppose that for every pair $u,v\in V$ the
single-vector bad event for the difference $u-v$ has probability at most
$2\exp(-k\varepsilon^2/8)$, that is,
\[
\mu\bigl\{\,\omega : \varepsilon\,\|u-v\|^2 < \bigl|\,\|A(\omega)(u-v)\|^2 -
\|u-v\|^2\,\bigr|\,\bigr\} \le 2\exp\!\bigl(-k\varepsilon^2/8\bigr).
\]
Then the probability of the bad-pair event — that some ordered pair $(u,v)\in V\times V$
fails the two-sided distortion bound $(1-\varepsilon)\|u-v\|^2 \le \|A(\omega)(u-v)\|^2
\le (1+\varepsilon)\|u-v\|^2$ — is at most
\[
  |V|^2 \cdot 2\exp\!\bigl(-k\varepsilon^2/8\bigr).
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Johnson–Lindenstrauss embedding from a Gaussian matrix]
\lean{johnson_lindenstrauss_of_gaussian}
\label{johnson_lindenstrauss_of_gaussian}
\leanok
\uses{BadPair, BadSingle, IsJLEmbedding, jl_concentration_single, jl_union_bound}
\difficulty{4}
Fix dimensions $d$ and $k$ with $k \ge 1$, a distortion parameter $\varepsilon \in
(0,1)$, and a finite set of points $V \subseteq \bbr^d$. Let $A$ be a random $k \times
d$ matrix whose entries $A_{ij}$ are independent Gaussian random variables, each with
mean $0$ and variance $1/k$. If the union-bound quantity satisfies
\[
  |V|^2 \cdot 2\exp\!\left(-\,k\varepsilon^2/8\right) < 1,
\]
then there exists a linear map $f : \bbr^d \to \bbr^k$ that is an $\varepsilon$-JL
embedding of $V$: for every pair $u, v \in V$,
\[
  (1-\varepsilon)\,\|u-v\|^2 \;\le\; \|f(u)-f(v)\|^2 \;\le\; (1+\varepsilon)\,\|u-v\|^2.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Sub-Gaussian random projections give a Johnson–Lindenstrauss embedding]
\lean{johnson_lindenstrauss_of_subgaussian}
\label{johnson_lindenstrauss_of_subgaussian}
\leanok
\uses{BadPair, BadSingle, IsJLEmbedding, concentration_zero, jl_concentration_single_subgaussian, jl_union_bound}
\difficulty{4}
Let $k \ge 1$, and let $A$ be a random $k \times d$ real matrix defined on a probability
space $(\Omega,\mu)$, so that for each $x \in \bbr^d$ the image $Ax \in \bbr^k$ has
coordinates $(Ax)_1,\dots,(Ax)_k$. Suppose that for every $x \in \bbr^d$ these $k$
coordinates are independent, and that each coordinate $(Ax)_i$ is sub-Gaussian with
variance proxy $\|x\|^2/k$, in the sense that $t \mapsto e^{t(Ax)_i}$ is integrable and
its moment generating function obeys $\E\!\left[e^{t(Ax)_i}\right] \le
\exp\!\bigl(\tfrac{\|x\|^2}{k}\cdot\tfrac{t^2}{2}\bigr)$ for all $t \in \bbr$, and
moreover has second moment $\E\!\left[(Ax)_i^2\right] = \|x\|^2/k$. Fix $0 < \varepsilon
< 1$ and a finite set $V \subseteq \bbr^d$ satisfying the union bound $|V|^2 \cdot
2\exp(-k\varepsilon^2/8) < 1$. Then there exists a linear map $f : \bbr^d \to \bbr^k$
that is an $\varepsilon$-JL embedding of $V$: for all $u,v \in V$,
\[
  (1-\varepsilon)\,\|u-v\|^2 \;\le\; \|f(u)-f(v)\|^2 \;\le\; (1+\varepsilon)\,\|u-v\|^2.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Measurability of the single-vector distortion event]
\lean{measurableSet_badSingle}
\label{measurableSet_badSingle}
\leanok
\uses{BadSingle}
\difficulty{4}
Fix a vector $x\in\bbr^d$ and a real number $\varepsilon$, and let
$(\Omega,\mathcal{F})$ be a measurable space. Suppose $A\colon\Omega\to\bbr^{k\times d}$
is a measurable map assigning to each $\omega$ a $k\times d$ real matrix $A(\omega)$.
Then the set of outcomes on which $x$ is badly distorted,
\[
\bigl\{\,\omega\in\Omega \;:\; \varepsilon\,\|x\|^2 < \bigl|\,\|A(\omega)\,x\|^2 -
\|x\|^2\,\bigr|\,\bigr\},
\]
is measurable.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Existence of a Gaussian matrix with independent entries]
\lean{exists_iid_gaussian_matrix}
\label{exists_iid_gaussian_matrix}
\leanok
\difficulty{6}
Let $k \ge 1$ and $d \ge 0$ be integers. Then there is a probability space $(\Omega,
\mathcal{F}, \mu)$ carrying a measurable map $\omega \mapsto A(\omega)$, valued in the
$k \times d$ real matrices, with the following properties: each entry $A_{ij}$, for $1
\le i \le k$ and $1 \le j \le d$, has law $\mathcal{N}(0, 1/k)$ (mean zero and variance
$1/k$); for each row index $i$ the family of entries $(A_{ij})_{j}$ is jointly
independent; and the family of rows $\bigl((A_{ij})_{j}\bigr)_{i}$ is jointly
independent.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Numerical failure-probability bound for Johnson–Lindenstrauss]
\lean{jl_failure_bound_of_dim}
\label{jl_failure_bound_of_dim}
\leanok
\difficulty{5}
Let $\varepsilon > 0$ and let $n \ge 2$ be an integer, and suppose the target dimension
$k$ satisfies $k \ge 32 \log n / \varepsilon^2$. Then for any finite set $V$ of points
in a Euclidean space with $\abs{V} \le n$, one has $k > 0$ and \[ \abs{V}^2 \cdot
2\exp\!\left(-\tfrac{k\varepsilon^2}{8}\right) < 1. \]
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Johnson–Lindenstrauss flattening lemma]
\lean{johnson_lindenstrauss}
\label{johnson_lindenstrauss}
\leanok
\uses{BadSingle, IsJLEmbedding, exists_iid_gaussian_matrix, jl_failure_bound_of_dim, johnson_lindenstrauss_of_gaussian, measurableSet_badSingle}
\difficulty{2}
Let $0 < \varepsilon < 1$ and let $n \ge 2$ be an integer. Suppose the target dimension
$k$ satisfies $k \ge 32\,\log n / \varepsilon^2$. Then for every finite set $V \subseteq
\bbr^d$ of at most $n$ points there exists a linear map $f : \bbr^d \to \bbr^k$ that is
an $\varepsilon$-JL embedding of $V$; that is,
\[
(1 - \varepsilon)\,\norm{u - v}^2 \;\le\; \norm{f(u) - f(v)}^2 \;\le\; (1 +
\varepsilon)\,\norm{u - v}^2
\]
for all $u, v \in V$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Johnson–Lindenstrauss flattening lemma]
\lean{johnson_lindenstrauss_subgaussian}
\label{johnson_lindenstrauss_subgaussian}
\leanok
\uses{BadSingle, IsJLEmbedding, hasSubgaussianMGF_row_proj, integral_sq_row_proj, jl_failure_bound_of_dim, johnson_lindenstrauss_of_subgaussian, measurableSet_badSingle, measurable_radMatrix, radJointMeasure, radMatrix, radMatrix_proj_indep, radMatrix_proj_meas}
\difficulty{3}
Let $0 < \varepsilon < 1$, let $n \ge 2$ be an integer, and let $k$ be a target
dimension satisfying $k \ge 32\,\log n / \varepsilon^2$. Then for every finite set $V$
of at most $n$ points in $\bbr^d$ there exists a linear map $f \colon \bbr^d \to \bbr^k$
such that every pair $u, v \in V$ has its squared distance preserved up to a factor
$\varepsilon$:
\[
(1 - \varepsilon)\,\|u - v\|^2 \;\le\; \|f(u) - f(v)\|^2 \;\le\; (1 + \varepsilon)\,\|u
- v\|^2.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Distance form of a JL embedding]
\lean{jl_dist_of_embedding}
\label{jl_dist_of_embedding}
\leanok
\uses{IsJLEmbedding, JLDistortion}
\difficulty{4}
Let $0 < \varepsilon < 1$, let $V$ be a finite set of points in $\bbr^d$, and let $f :
\bbr^d \to \bbr^k$ be a linear map that is an $\varepsilon$-JL embedding of $V$, so that
for every pair $u, v \in V$ one has $(1-\varepsilon)\,\|u-v\|^2 \le \|f(u)-f(v)\|^2 \le
(1+\varepsilon)\,\|u-v\|^2$. Then for all $u, v \in V$,
\[
\sqrt{1-\varepsilon}\,\|u - v\| \;\le\; \|f(u) - f(v)\| \;\le\;
\sqrt{1+\varepsilon}\,\|u - v\|.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Johnson–Lindenstrauss flattening in distance form]
\lean{johnson_lindenstrauss_dist}
\label{johnson_lindenstrauss_dist}
\leanok
\uses{jl_dist_of_embedding, johnson_lindenstrauss}
\difficulty{1}
Let $\varepsilon \in (0,1)$ and let $n \ge 2$ be an integer, and suppose the target
dimension $k$ satisfies $k \ge 32\,\log n / \varepsilon^2$. Then for every finite set $V
\subseteq \bbr^d$ of at most $n$ points there exists a linear map $f : \bbr^d \to
\bbr^k$ such that, for all $u, v \in V$,
\[
\sqrt{1-\varepsilon}\,\norm{u - v} \;\le\; \norm{f(u) - f(v)} \;\le\;
\sqrt{1+\varepsilon}\,\norm{u - v},
\]
where $\norm{\cdot}$ denotes the Euclidean norm.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Johnson–Lindenstrauss flattening: distance form]
\lean{johnson_lindenstrauss_subgaussian_dist}
\label{johnson_lindenstrauss_subgaussian_dist}
\leanok
\uses{jl_dist_of_embedding, johnson_lindenstrauss_subgaussian}
\difficulty{1}
Let $\varepsilon \in (0,1)$ and let $n \ge 2$ be an integer. Suppose $k$ is a natural
number with $k \ge 32\,(\log n)/\varepsilon^2$, and let $V$ be a finite set of at most
$n$ points in $\bbr^d$. Then there exists a linear map $f : \bbr^d \to \bbr^k$ such that
for all $u, v \in V$,
\[
\sqrt{1-\varepsilon}\,\norm{u-v} \;\le\; \norm{f(u)-f(v)} \;\le\;
\sqrt{1+\varepsilon}\,\norm{u-v}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Existence of a Johnson–Lindenstrauss dimension threshold]
\lean{johnson_lindenstrauss_dim_bound}
\label{johnson_lindenstrauss_dim_bound}
\leanok
\uses{IsJLEmbedding, johnson_lindenstrauss}
\difficulty{2}
Let $\varepsilon$ be a real number with $0 < \varepsilon < 1$, and let $n \ge 2$ be an
integer. Then there is a threshold $k_0 \in \bbn$ such that for every target dimension
$k \ge k_0$, every ambient dimension $d$, and every finite set $V \subseteq \bbr^d$ of
at most $n$ points, there exists a linear map $f : \bbr^d \to \bbr^k$ that is an
$\varepsilon$-JL embedding of $V$; that is, for all $u, v \in V$,
\[
(1 - \varepsilon)\,\norm{u - v}^2 \;\le\; \norm{f(u) - f(v)}^2 \;\le\; (1 +
\varepsilon)\,\norm{u - v}^2.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Dimension threshold for Johnson–Lindenstrauss embeddings]
\lean{johnson_lindenstrauss_subgaussian_dim_bound}
\label{johnson_lindenstrauss_subgaussian_dim_bound}
\leanok
\uses{IsJLEmbedding, johnson_lindenstrauss_subgaussian}
\difficulty{2}
Fix a distortion parameter $\varepsilon$ with $0 < \varepsilon < 1$ and an integer $n
\ge 2$. Then there is a threshold $k_0 \in \bbn$ such that for every target dimension $k
\ge k_0$, every source dimension $d$, and every finite set $V \subseteq \bbr^d$ of at
most $n$ points, there exists a linear map $f : \bbr^d \to \bbr^k$ that is an
$\varepsilon$-JL embedding of $V$: that is, $(1-\varepsilon)\,\|u - v\|^2 \le \|f(u) -
f(v)\|^2 \le (1+\varepsilon)\,\|u - v\|^2$ for all $u, v \in V$.
\end{theorem}
